items.title: Bobby Hutcherson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: He said, 'John, open up the back of the van to check it out.'

ctx.x: How long did it take for you to get your facility back?

Really it took a year, but all that time I was still playing. I’d just wrap tape on my hand and play. There was no way I was going to stop playing. One time when I’m working at Keystone Korner, I’m driving my van. I heard this loud explosion. I’m driving down Van Ness street. Boom. So I’m driving, looking all around, trying to see what’s going on. I get on the freeway. I start driving home, and I see all these cops. I see the SWAT team. They’re behind me. They pull up. What’s going on? “Pull over on the next turn…

vibes are in the back of the van here.” He said, “John, open up the back of the van to check it out.” He opens it up and says, “Yeah, there’s some weird looking instrument sitting back here.” He says, “Wow. Jeez, you guys. We got the wrong guy.” He said, “Bobby, I’m really sorry. Come on, you guys. Let’s go.” So right – they’re all about to get in their cars, and all of a sudden the good cop, he says, “Oh.” He starts walking back, and he says, “Bobby” – he’s got a pen and a piece of paper.
